Chapter 6 • Covariant Derivative

6.4 Torsion and Curvature

  • The torsion of a connection \(\nabla\) is the \((1,2)\)-tensor field6 \begin{align*} \mathtt{T} : \Gamma T^*\mathcal{M} \times \Gamma T\mathcal{M} \times \Gamma T\mathcal{M} &\longrightarrow C^\infty(\mathcal{M}) \\ (\mathsf{X}, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) &\longmapsto \mathtt{T}(\mathsf{X}, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) \coloneqq \mathsf{X}\left\lceil \nabla_\mathcal{X} \mathcal{Y} - \nabla_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{X} - [\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}] \right\rfloor, \end{align*} where the commutator of two vector fields is the vector field \begin{align*} [\cdot, \cdot] : \Gamma T\mathcal{M} \times \Gamma T\mathcal{M} &\longrightarrow \Gamma T\mathcal{M} \\ (\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) &\longmapsto [\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}], \quad [\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}]\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \coloneqq \mathcal{X}\left\lfloor \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \right\rceil - \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor \mathcal{X}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \right\rceil. \end{align*} From now on, whenever a single chart is involved, we drop the chart label, \(\Gamma \equiv \Gamma_\mathscr{X}\). Since \([\partial x_j, \partial x_k] = 0\)7, the components of the torsion read \[ \mathtt{T}^i_{jk} \coloneqq \mathtt{T}(dx^i, \partial x_j, \partial x_k) = dx^i\left\lceil \nabla_{\partial x_j} \partial x_k - \nabla_{\partial x_k} \partial x_j \right\rfloor = \Gamma^i_{kj} - \Gamma^i_{jk}. \]

  • An affine manifold \((\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}, \mathcal{A}, \nabla)\) is torsion free if \(\mathtt{T} = 0\), i.e. if \[ \nabla_\mathcal{X} \mathcal{Y} - \nabla_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{X} = [\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}] \qquad \forall \, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y} \in \Gamma T\mathcal{M}, \] which, in any chart, amounts to the symmetry \(\Gamma^i_{jk} = \Gamma^i_{kj}\) of the connection coefficient functions. For a torsion-free connection, the normal coordinates constructed above therefore make all the connection coefficient functions vanish at the chosen point \(p\).

  • The Riemann curvature of a connection \(\nabla\) is the \((1,3)\)-tensor field8 \begin{align*} \mathrm{Riem} : \Gamma T^*\mathcal{M} \times \Gamma T\mathcal{M} \times \Gamma T\mathcal{M} \times \Gamma T\mathcal{M} &\longrightarrow C^\infty(\mathcal{M}) \\ (\mathsf{X}, \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) &\longmapsto \mathrm{Riem}(\mathsf{X}, \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) \\ &\coloneqq \mathsf{X}\left\lceil \nabla_\mathcal{X} \nabla_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{Z} - \nabla_\mathcal{Y} \nabla_\mathcal{X} \mathcal{Z} - \nabla_{[\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}]} \mathcal{Z} \right\rfloor. \end{align*} Its components follow from \(\nabla_{\partial x_m} \partial x_j = \Gamma^r_{jm} \, \partial x_r\), the product rule and \([\partial x_k, \partial x_m] = 0\): \begin{align*} \mathrm{Riem}^i_{jkm} &\coloneqq \mathrm{Riem}(dx^i, \partial x_j, \partial x_k, \partial x_m) = dx^i\left\lceil \nabla_{\partial x_k} \big( \Gamma^r_{jm} \, \partial x_r \big) - \nabla_{\partial x_m} \big( \Gamma^r_{jk} \, \partial x_r \big) \right\rfloor \\ &= \partial x_k\left\lfloor \Gamma^i_{jm} \right\rceil - \partial x_m\left\lfloor \Gamma^i_{jk} \right\rceil + \Gamma^i_{rk} \, \Gamma^r_{jm} - \Gamma^i_{rm} \, \Gamma^r_{jk}. \end{align*} The Riemann curvature is antisymmetric in its last two indices, \(\mathrm{Riem}^i_{jkm} = -\mathrm{Riem}^i_{jmk}\). For a torsion-free connection it satisfies the (differential) Bianchi identity \[ (\nabla_\mathcal{W} \mathrm{Riem})(\mathsf{X}, \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) + (\nabla_\mathcal{X} \mathrm{Riem})(\mathsf{X}, \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}, \mathcal{W}) + (\nabla_\mathcal{Y} \mathrm{Riem})(\mathsf{X}, \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{W}, \mathcal{X}) = 0, \] for all \(\mathsf{X} \in \Gamma T^*\mathcal{M}\) and \(\mathcal{W}, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}, \mathcal{Z} \in \Gamma T\mathcal{M}\), or, in components, \[ \big( \nabla_{\partial x_n} \mathrm{Riem} \big)^i_{jkm} + \big( \nabla_{\partial x_k} \mathrm{Riem} \big)^i_{jmn} + \big( \nabla_{\partial x_m} \mathrm{Riem} \big)^i_{jnk} = 0. \]

  • The Ricci curvature of a connection \(\nabla\) is the \((0,2)\)-tensor field obtained by contracting the upper index of the Riemann curvature with its third slot, \[ \mathrm{Ric}(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) \coloneqq \mathrm{Riem}(dx^m, \mathcal{X}, \partial x_m, \mathcal{Y}), \] where the sum over \(m\) does not depend on the chart employed9. Its components are \(\mathrm{Ric}_{ab} \coloneqq \mathrm{Ric}(\partial x_a, \partial x_b) = \mathrm{Riem}^m_{amb}\). Note that, for a general connection, the Ricci curvature need not be symmetric.

6

That the right-hand side is \(C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\)-linear in every argument is not obvious, since \(\nabla_\mathcal{X} \mathcal{Y}\) alone is not: by the product rule, \(\nabla_\mathcal{X}(g\,\mathcal{Y}) - \nabla_{g\mathcal{Y}} \mathcal{X} = \mathcal{X}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil \mathcal{Y} + g \big( \nabla_\mathcal{X}\mathcal{Y} - \nabla_\mathcal{Y}\mathcal{X} \big)\), while \([\mathcal{X}, g\,\mathcal{Y}] = \mathcal{X}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil \mathcal{Y} + g \, [\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}]\), so the non-tensorial terms \(\mathcal{X}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil \mathcal{Y}\) cancel.

7

\([\partial x_j, \partial x_k]\left\lfloor f \right\rceil = \Big( \partial_j \partial_k \left[ f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \right] - \partial_k \partial_j \left[ f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \right] \Big) \circ \mathscr{X} = 0\), by Schwarz’s theorem.

8

As for the torsion, the non-tensorial terms produced by the product rule cancel, here against those coming from \(\nabla_{[\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}]} \mathcal{Z}\).

9

Under a change of chart, the Jacobian factors coming from \(dy^m\) and from \(\partial y_m\) combine into \(\frac{\partial \mathscr{Y}^m}{\partial \mathscr{X}^a} \frac{\partial \mathscr{X}^b}{\partial \mathscr{Y}^m} = \delta^b_a\).
